column3: Near-verbatim parallel: Musa is called at the fire in a blessed setting, and Allah is named Lord of the worlds.
The followers of poets do not clarify the Sinai call, its place, or its speaker.
Its divine blessings clarify blessing as a bestowed good, but not the Sinai encounter.
It closely repeats Musa's arrival and the call addressed to him, supplying the immediate parallel scene.
The preceding verse gives Musa's arrival at the fire from which the focus call begins.
The agricultural image does not add to the calling, blessed place, or tree.
It identifies the caller as Musa's Lord and the valley as holy, closely illuminating the focus setting.
The later notice about revelation at Midian gives only broad continuity for the Musa narrative.
It names the Lord as blessed, supporting the focus's blessing language at a general level.
It directly recalls the Lord calling Musa in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
Its metaphorical wandering through valleys does not explain the blessed valley.
